title: refactor: remove Zerion as a balances API provider
description:
## Summary

- `/portfolio` now serves all Zerion data, so Zerion is no longer needed in the `/balances` (or `/collectibles`) endpoint.
- The Zerion fallback for counterfactual safes and the Zerion collectibles path were dead code — Datadog shows zero production traffic to them. Counterfactual safes now return a 404 from `/balances` instead of Zerion data.
- Deletes the unused `ZerionBalancesApi` service, its collectibles entity/builder, and the dead integration specs.
- Kept: `zerion-balance.entity`, `zerion-api.helpers`, and the wallet-portfolio service, which `/portfolio` and `/positions` still use.

## Related

- [WA-2753](https://linear.app/safe-global/issue/WA-2753/remove-zerion-as-an-api-provider-from-the-balances-endpoint)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

findings.claim: The `safeAddress` parameter on `IBalancesApiManager.getApi` is still declared as required even though the implementation no longer uses it (renamed to `_safeAddress`), so every caller and test still has to generate a fake address just to satisfy a signature that no longer needs it.
In `getFiatCodes`, wrapping the result in `rawify` is redundant because `IPricesApi.getFiatCodes()` already returns `Raw<Array<string>>`, making the call an unnecessary no-op cast.

The `features.counterfactualBalances` flag (`FF_COUNTERFACTUAL_BALANCES`) has no remaining consumer since `BalancesApiManager` no longer reads it, but the env var, its `.env.sample.json` entry, the `.vscode/launch.json` override, and the `counterfactualBalances: true/false` toggles in several integration specs are still present, which could mislead future readers into thinking a counterfactual code path still exists.

The integration suite does not assert the new behavior described in the PR body where counterfactual safes return a 404 from `/balances`, so this intentional user-visible change is not locked in or documented by a test.
The describe block named `getApi checks` (under `Balances API Manager Tests`) no longer reflects what it tests, since Zerion is no longer part of the routing decision.
The two remaining `getApi` tests still generate a `safeAddress` value even though there is no longer any branch coverage that depends on it, leaving unnecessary test setup.
